name: Isolated Jejuno-Ileal Duplication

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiologic Diagnostic Criteria for Jejuno-Ileal Duplication

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic or tubular structure contiguous with the jejunum or ileum on imaging or surgery
Histological confirmation of a shared smooth muscle wall between the duplication and native bowel
Presence of gastrointestinal mucosal lining within the duplication cyst
Symptoms such as abdominal distension, vomiting, or intestinal obstruction
No associated duplications or malformations in other segments of the gastrointestinal tract

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a cystic or tubular structure contiguous with jejunum or ileum plus histological confirmation of shared muscular wall and mucosal lining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by surgical and histopathological findings; imaging is supportive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal cystic mass palpable on examination
Intestinal obstruction due to duplication cyst

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal bleeding from ectopic gastric mucosa
searchTerms: gut bleeding from misplaced stomach tissue
intestinal bleeding from ectopic gastric lining
GI bleeding from abnormal stomach tissue

occasional.symptomName: Fever due to secondary infection or abscess formation

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as expected

rare.symptomName: Perforation of duplication cyst causing peritonitis
searchTerms: hole in cyst causing belly infection

rare.symptomName: Intussusception caused by duplication cyst acting as lead point

laboratory: Leukocytosis in case of infection or perforation
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic mass adjacent to jejunum or ileum
CT scan demonstrating cystic or tubular duplication with shared wall
Contrast studies revealing filling defects or obstruction
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Histopathology confirming shared muscular wall and mucosal lining

distinguishingFeatures: True diverticulum arising from antimesenteric border of ileum
Contains all layers of bowel wall but no shared muscular wall with adjacent bowel
Usually located within 60 cm of ileocecal valve
Cystic lesion not contiguous with bowel lumen
No shared muscular wall with adjacent bowel
Usually asymptomatic unless large or infected

references: Stringer MD. Gastrointestinal duplications. Semin Pediatr Surg. 1995;4(2):104-109.
Puligandla PS, et al. Gastrointestinal duplications. J Pediatr Surg. 2003;38(5):740-744.
